Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=7}}, he primarily plays at the [[point guard]] position, but he can also play as a [[shooting guard]] or [[small forward]] due to his height and wingspan. ==Professional career== ===USK Praha (2007–2009)=== [[File:Tomas Satoransky 2018 Wizards.jpg|thumb|Satoranský with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2018]] From 2007 to 2009, Satoranský played with [[USK Praha]]. ===Sevilla (2009–2014)=== In 2009, Satoranský signed with [[CB Sevilla]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB|ACB League]], where he played for the next five seasons. He was selected in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] (32nd overall) by the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://basket.idnes.cz/draft-nba-2012-cx3-/nba.aspx?c=A120628_224646_nba_ten|title=Satoranský je čtvrtým Čechem v NBA. Jde do Washingtonu za Veselým — iDNES.cz|access-date=29 June 2012}} He played at the 2012 NBA Summer League.{{cite web|last=Standig|first=Ben|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/washington-wizards/tomas-satoransky-timing-was-right-wizards-nba-dreams|title=Tomas Satoransky: Timing was right for Wizards, NBA dreams|website=NBC Sports Washington|date=22 July 2016|access-date=4 November 2019}} ===FC Barcelona (2014–2016)=== In July 2014, Satoranský signed a two-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona Lassa]].{{cite news|title=FC Barcelona lands guard Satoransky|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138255|access-date=11 July 2014|work=Euroleague.net}} In July 2016, he parted ways with Barcelona in order to join the NBA.{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/sections/basketball/first-team/news/2016-2017/tomas-satoransky-leaves-fc-barcelona-lassa|title=Tomas Satoransky leaves FC Barcelona Lassa|publisher=fcbarcelona.com|date=4 July 2016|access-date=8 July 2016}} ===Washington Wizards (2016–2019)=== [[File:Tomas Satoransky (32868537347) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Tomáš Satoranský being interviewed in 2018]] On 21 July 2016, Satoranský signed with the Washington Wizards.{{cite news|title=Wizards Sign Tomas Satoransky|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/07/21/wizards-sign-tomas-satoransky|access-date=21 July 2016|work=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=21 July 2016}} On 1 December 2017, he scored a career-high 17 points in a 109–91 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975071|title=Morris, Satoransky lead Wizards to 109-91 rout of Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=1 December 2017|access-date=2 December 2017}} On 3 February 2018, he set a new career high with 19 points in a 115–98 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975524|title=Porter, Wizards ease to 115-98 victory over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=3 February 2018|access-date=4 February 2018}} He surpassed that mark a week later, scoring 25 points on 10-of-12 shooting in a 101–90 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975575|title=Tomas Satoransky scores 25, Wizards beat Bulls 101-90|work=ESPN.com|date=10 February 2018|access-date=11 February 2018}} On 11 January 2019, he recorded his first career triple-double with 18 points, a career-high 12 rebounds and 10 assists in a 113–106 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071298|title=Beal scores 32, Wizards top Giannis-less Bucks 113-106|work=ESPN.com|date=11 January 2019|access-date=11 January 2019}} ===Chicago Bulls (2019–2021)=== On 6 July 2019, Satoranský was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a [[sign-and-trade]] deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release-title|title=BULLS ACQUIRE TOMAS SATORANSKY|work=NBA.com|date=6 July 2019}} On 6 January 2020, Satoranský logged 11 points, 5 rebounds and a career-high 14 assists in a 110–118 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=Bulls vs. Mavericks - Game Recap - January 6, 2020 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161187|access-date=2021-04-05|website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web|title=Chicago Bulls vs. Dallas Mavericks Score and Stats - January 6, 2020 Gametracker|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/recap/NBA_20200106_CHI@DAL/|access-date=2021-04-05|website=CBSSports.com}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2021–2022)=== On 8 August 2021, Satoranský was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], along with [[Garrett Temple]] and draft picks, for [[Lonzo Ball]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-tomas-satoransky-garrett-temple-chicago-bulls |title=Pelicans acquire Tomáš Satoranský and Garrett Temple |date=8 August 2021 |work=NBA.com}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2022)=== On 8 February 2022, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] acquired Satoranský, [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]], [[Josh Hart]], [[Didi Louzada]], a protected 2022 first-round draft pick, the better of New Orleans’ and Portland's 2026 second-round draft picks and New Orleans' 2027 second-round draft pick from the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[CJ McCollum]], [[Larry Nance Jr.]] and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]].{{Cite press release|date=8 February 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=TRAIL BLAZERS COMPLETE TRADE WITH NEW ORLEANS|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers}} A day later, Satoranský was traded yet again, this time to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade.{{Cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS COMPLETE THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-three-team-trade|access-date=9 February 2022|website=NBA}} He played one game for the Spurs before agreeing to a contract buyout on 26 February 2022. ===Return to Washington (2022)=== On 28 February 2022, Satoranský signed a rest-of-season contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{ cite web|url=https://wtop.com/washington-wizards/2022/02/wizards-sign-satoransky-for-second-stint-with-washington/|website=wtop.com|title=Wizards sign Satoransky for second stint with Washington|access-date=28 February 2022|date=28 February 2022}} ===Return to FC Barcelona (2022–2026)=== On 4 July 2022, Satoranský penned a four-year deal with his former club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]], joining his national squad teammate [[Jan Veselý]] under the guidance of coach [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]].{{Cite web |title=Tomas Satoransky returns to Barça! |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/2666291/tomas-satoransky-returns-to-barca |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=www.fcbarcelona.com}} The team would be crowned champions of the [[2022–23 ACB season|2022–23 ACB]] after beating [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the [[2023 ACB Playoffs#Finals|finals]], with Satoranský winning the first national title in his career.{{Cite web |title=¡Un Barça colosal conquista la Liga Endesa 2022-23! (82-93) |url=https://www.acb.com/partido/ver/id/103536 |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=www.acb.com |language=es}} After the retirement of [[Álex Abrines]] in July 2025, Satoranský became [[team captain]] of FC Barcelona.{{Cite web |title=Satoransky, Laprovittola i Parra son els tres capitans del Barça 2025/26 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.cat/ca/basquet/primer-equip/noticies/4365099/satoransky-laprovittola-i-parra-son-els-tres-capitans-del-barca-202526/featured |date=2025-09-18 |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=www.fcbarcelona.cat |language=ca}} On June 30, 2026, Satoranský left Barcelona upon the expiration of his contract.{{cite web | title=Tomas Satoransky ends his second spell with Barça | url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4528786/tomas-satoransky-ends-his-second-spell-with-barca | website=fcbarcelona.com | date=30 June 2026 | access-date=30 June 2026 }} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2026–present)=== On July 15, 2026, Satoranský signed a one-year deal with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/hapoel-adds-playmaking-pedigree-by-signing-satoransky/|title=Hapoel adds playmaking pedigree by signing Satoransky|date=July 15, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 15, 2026}} ==National team career== Satoranský has played in all of the age categories for the [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|Czech Republic]] national basketball team. He joined the senior national team for the first time during [[FIBA EuroBasket 2009 qualification|EuroBasket 2009 qualifiers]]. In 2010, he played at the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], with the Czech Republic Under-20 junior national team. Satoranský has also represented the Czech senior national team at [[EuroBasket 2013]] and [[EuroBasket 2015]].[http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2013.roundID_8722.teamID_2612.playerID_57967.html EuroBasket 2013 profile][http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_%7Bd166e39e-2323-4863-b229-76357a926fa2%7D.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_2612.playerID_57967.html EuroBasket 2015 profile] He also played at [[EuroBasket 2017]], and helped the Czech Republic qualify to the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]] for the first time.[https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/player/Tomas-Satoransky EuroBasket 2017 profile]{{cite web|title=Czech Republic's Satoransky on making the World Cup|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/european-qualifiers/news/czech-republics-satoransky-the-boys-have-grown-up-which-makes-us-one-of-the-best-teams-weve-ever-had|access-date=19 September 2018}}[http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/player/Tomas-Satoransky 2019 FIBA World Cup profile] Satoransky scored 14 points in a loss to [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in the preliminary round of the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympics]] in Tokyo. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA
